# Anivora 0.1.36 — Native playback, player controls and mini-player

- Attempt bounded, cancellable on-device media URL extraction before using an embedded provider player. Play extracted HLS/DASH/MP4 natively; retain a one-time page fallback if native playback fails. No episode bytes are proxied through Render.
- Use one Th3-style toolbar with Cast/Auto and one tightly aligned timeline/transport row. Disable native video controls and suppress provider transports before their first visible video frame; replace provider token/decryption chrome with Anivora's loading state.
- Remove the top video/hero/trailer gap while keeping tappable controls clear of system bars.
- Keep a draggable in-app mini-player over Home and detail navigation, with pause/play, expand and close. Use Android system PiP for native playback outside the app; true page-only fallback uses the in-app mini-player instead of claiming unsupported system PiP.
- Defer explicit Cast decisions while a provider initializes/discovers media. Compatible public HTTPS streams can use Cast; true embeds and header/cookie-bound sources still show their restriction.
- Preserve download-first playback, native HLS/parts/merge and manga providers, remote avatars, the top-right Profile TV pairing entry, server notices, Cloudflare pages, package and signed GitHub APK updates.

Android version code: **38**, newer than 0.1.35/code 37. Package:
`com.brandon300.anivora`. ARM64, Android 7.0/API 24 or newer. Preserve the existing
signing certificate and install over the existing app without uninstalling.

## Validation and limits

Release gates cover TypeScript, lint, Expo compatibility, app/API tests, native
JVM policy/download regressions, Android 14 download/HLS integration, exact
compiled source, signature/package/version and public APK checksum. Controlled
browser checks inspect timeline spacing, early provider control suppression and
mini-player navigation. The release includes its exact source commit and SHA-256.

Physical Infinix Hot 50i, real Chromecast and live-provider PiP QA are pending;
no device certification is claimed. Provider extraction can fail or require
phone-only headers; native playback alone does not make every source Castable.
Local/downloaded files remain ineligible for Cast. True WebView-only mini playback
can reload at its measured position and pauses outside the app.
TV pairing still needs the running API/database and a future compatible TV client;
no Android TV app is included. A phone update cannot lift a Render billing suspension.

See [player behavior and limits](player-chrome.md), [Cast](casting.md),
[TV pairing](tv-pairing.md), and [0.1.35 notes](releases/0.1.35.md).
